negative_results: A REAL_DEVICE clock acquires NOTHING: no timebase hardware (oscillator, counter, GPSDO, phase comparator) exists here, so a real read raises NoClockHardwareError and its receipt is PREREGISTERED_NOT_RUN.
Clock jitter raises a tone's noise floor; that raised floor is a KNOWN_ORDINARY_EFFECT, not a signal. refuse_jitter_as_signal raises (via the governance core's noise-to-resonance refusal).
An unknown transport latency stays uncertain: without a reference delay the absolute latency carries a cycle ambiguity and transport_latency returns an interval with resolved=False.

Every one of the eight fault modes (clipping, drift, saturation, packet loss, missing samples, cycle slip, glitch, holdover) demonstrably alters the clean synthetic reading and is deterministic under the seed.

A synthetic clock is never a measured one (refuse_synthetic_clock_as_measured), and a synthetic fractional frequency offset is never read as relativistic time dilation when the sensitivity is insufficient (refuse_relativistic_interpretation).
A ClockAcquisition cannot carry a measurement claim class: constructing one with PHYSICAL_MEASUREMENT invokes refuse_synthetic_as_physical.
No physical measurement was performed; measured_here is nothing and PHYSICAL_VALIDATION_NOT_CLAIMED.
reopening_test: Reopen the clock/phase lane if: a REAL_DEVICE clock ever returns samples instead of blocking; a jitter-raised noise floor is ever classified as a signal, tone or resonance; a transport latency is reported as resolved without a supplied reference delay; a common-clock closure residual fails to be far below the independent-oscillator residual for the same jitter; a planted phase, integer skew, drift or jitter fails to be recovered from the deterministic synthetic clock; or any reading is emitted at a class above SYNTHETIC_OBSERVATION. A physical clock/phase run is reopened only when built, calibrated timebase hardware with a captured raw artifact, a clock binding, an environment log and an uncertainty budget exists.
